title: Asterion Health - Renewal & Residency Capacity Sync
summary: Check-in to align on Asterion's renewal window, plan for committed capacity increase, and evaluate EU on-prem deployment and data residency constraints. Action items include sharing EU on-prem runbook, updated pricing scenarios, and scheduling a short performance benchmark next week.
action_items: Sarah Miller: Send EU on-prem architecture runbook and cost scenarios by 2026-06-08
Diego Ramos: Prepare a short benchmark checklist (latency/throughput/KV cache behavior) and proposed test dataset by 2026-06-09
Nadia Ivanov (Asterion): Share specific compliance checklist items (data retention, key management) by 2026-06-07
Priya Patel: Draft proposed renewal amendment with 12 month commitment and burst tier options by 2026-06-10
next_steps: Schedule 30m benchmark run next Tue/Thu - Diego to coordinate with Ethan
Sarah to share pricing scenarios for 12/24 month terms with committed units + burst
Security docs transfer - Asterion to review Redwood SOC2 + KMS integration notes
Follow-up call week of 2026-06-15 to review benchmark results and finalize amendment
transcript: [00:00] Sarah Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro from our side, Diego is our solutions engineer, Priya is your CSM; we'll keep this focused on the renewal and the EU on-prem ask.

[00:12] Maya Chen: Thanks Sarah. Quick context — our current contract ends late July, and with the new clinical pipeline we need higher committed throughput plus EU data residency for a subset of PHI-like logs.
[00:25] Tom Briscoe: Yeah we've been running some spikes, noticed latency tail at 2nd half of day in EU region and want to understand Dedicated vs Private options and cost tradeoffs.
[00:38] Diego Ramos: Got it. For clarity, when you say Private, do you mean Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem package) or a Dedicated cluster in our EU region?

[00:45] Tom Briscoe: Ideally Private — we have compliance that requires keys to be in our KMS and certain audit flows not leaving the VPC, but we want the control plane to remain with Redwood if possible.

[00:55] Nadia Ivanov: Right. Our security team listed three hard requirements: SSO with SAML, KMS integration for model request encryption keys, and audit logs retained for 7 years. Also data residency — certain request logs must stay in EU.

[01:12] Sarah Miller: That's helpful. We support SSO/SAML and KMS integrations on Private; audit logs retention is an add-on but we can build a retention policy into the Private offering. We'll share the runbook that shows network topology and KMS flow.

[01:25] Maya Chen: Cool. On capacity — currently we have 4 reserved GPU units for prod and burst enabled. We anticipate 2.5x increase in token volume next quarter if AA release goes live. We need options for committed + burst and what the price delta is.

[01:40] Diego Ramos: Two levers: increase reserved capacity (predictable tps) or keep current reserved and raise burst limits (pay-as-you-go). Reserved lowers unit cost but requires a term commitment. We can run some cost scenarios for 12 vs 24 months.
[01:53] Tom Briscoe: What's the practical lead time for Private EU on-prem? Any idea of onboarding window?

[02:00] Diego Ramos: Typical path: 4-6 weeks for Private VPC with our standard images + KMS hookup, longer for fully on-prem air-gapped installs. For EU on-prem with your infra team cooperating I'd estimate 6-10 weeks; dedicated (hosted in our EU cluster) is faster — 1-2 weeks for provisioning.

[02:15] Sarah Miller: That's why many customers pick a hybrid: dedicated for immediate throughput, then migrate sensitive workloads to Private over a controlled cutover. There's also a canary routing option so you can split traffic by tag.
[02:27] Nadia Ivanov: Canary routing sounds good, but we need guarantees around where the KV cache lives and how tokens are stored — anything that could leak PHI needs to be resident in EU.

[02:38] Diego Ramos: KV cache for Private will be in your VPC; for dedicated hosted variants we can set region-level residency but not customer-controlled KMS. We'll outline the exact cache and data flow in the runbook.
[02:50] Ethan Li: From SRE perspective, do you support cross-region failover? We need to know RTO and how state is transferred during failover.

[02:58] Priya Patel: Yes, cross-region failover is supported with automatic fallback policies; RTO varies by deployment model — for dedicated it's typically under a minute for stateless routing, with KV warmups adding to tail latency. We'll include expected numbers.

[03:13] Maya Chen: Let's talk success metrics for the pilot. We're primarily concerned with 95th percentile latency below 300ms for prompts under 1024 tokens, and cost per 1k tokens not exceeding X (they didn't say exact number).

[03:27] Diego Ramos: Okay we'll build a benchmark plan: latency percentiles, throughput qps, and KV cache hit rates. We'll propose a small dataset that mirrors your AA pipeline and run a short 2-hour soak.
[03:40] Tom Briscoe: Great. On contract terms — if we commit to an uplift (say double reserved capacity) for 12 months, what's the savings vs pure on-demand?

[03:50] Sarah Miller: Roughly 25-35% lower unit cost on committed vs burst depending on model family and quantization profile. I'll send exact pricing scenarios for 12 and 24 month terms, including a hybrid committed + burst structure.
[04:02] Maya Chen: Are there any penalties if we exceed committed units often? We want elasticity without surprise invoices.

[04:07] Priya Patel: We include a buffer and can tier overage pricing; also we recommend dashboards and alerts so you'll see utilization. We can also add a monthly reconciliation to adjust committed units if usage sustains.
[04:20] Nadia Ivanov: On security artifacts — can you provide SOC2 report and a data flow diagram? Also we need details on key rotation and HSM support.

[04:28] Sarah Miller: Yes we will attach SOC2, and Diego will include the KMS/HSM integration details in the runbook. Key rotation is customer-controlled for Private (via your KMS), and for dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key for certain plans.
[04:40] Diego Ramos: Note — for on-prem air-gapped we do a different signing and image verification step; I can call that out explicitly so your security team sees it.
[04:47] Ethan Li: If we go with a hybrid route, how disruptive is cutover? We can't afford long downtime during migration.

[04:53] Diego Ramos: The migration is traffic-shifted canary style with gradual ramp to minimize disruption. We keep dual serving capacity during the cutover so there is no single big downtime event; typical cutovers are under 2 hours of ramping but require pre-warmed KV caches.
[05:08] Maya Chen: Pre-warming KV cache — what's the best way to do that? Does Redwood provide tooling to replay prefix contexts?

[05:15] Diego Ramos: We provide a pre-warm tool that replays a curated set of request prefixes and warms shared cache. We'll include runbook steps for that; you'll need to coordinate traffic mirroring briefly.
[05:25] Tom Briscoe: About billing — can we get monthly metrics broken down by route/model/token so we can attribute costs to product teams?
[05:32] Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdowns and per-token cost reporting. We can enable token-level tagging for your routes and export CSVs to your billing system.
[05:43] Maya Chen: Perfect. Now on timeline — our leadership wants a go/no-go on renewal uplift by 2026-06-25 to include in Q3 budgeting. Is that feasible for Redwood?
[05:53] Sarah Miller: Yes, that's feasible. We'll prioritize runbook and cost scenarios so you can review. If the benchmark looks good, we can have an amendment drafted the following week.
[06:02] Nadia Ivanov: One more on compliance: do you have EU data residency guarantee language we can include in SOW?
[06:08] Sarah Miller: We can include residency clauses for Private and for dedicated EU clusters; we'll propose SLA verbiage for data locality in the amendment.
[06:15] Maya Chen: For the benchmark next week, what do you need from us?
[06:20] Diego Ramos: A couple things: a small representative input corpus (anonymized), a shortlist of models you want to test, and a point of contact for access. I'll email a checklist.
[06:29] Ethan Li: I'll coordinate the dataset and provide infra contacts. We'll prefer Tue morning or Thu afternoon for the run — timezone CET.
[06:36] Sarah Miller: Noted. Diego, can you also include a quick script we can run to capture tail latency and KV hit rates?
[06:42] Diego Ramos: Yep, small harness with a k6-like runner and metrics export. I'll attach the harness and expected thresholds.
[06:49] Tom Briscoe: If the benchmark passes, what's the procurement timeline for the amendment?
[06:53] Priya Patel: Typically 1-2 weeks for sign-off on a standard amendment once legal reviews; for enterprise terms it can be a bit longer. We'll loop in Redwood Legal early if you want.
[07:02] Maya Chen: We will. Any red flags we haven't discussed?
[07:06] Sarah Miller: Only that air-gapped on-prem will take longer and require extra security review; otherwise the path is straightforward. We'll document risks in the runbook.
[07:14] Nadia Ivanov: Also confirm backup retention and who handles incident response in Private deployment.
[07:18] Diego Ramos: For Private, backup retention policies are customer-configurable; incident response is collaborative — Redwood provides runbooks and will support for an agreed SLA tier.

[07:27] Maya Chen: Alright that helps. Let's recap next steps — Diego will send benchmark checklist, Sarah will send pricing scenarios and runbook, Nadia will send compliance checklist, Priya will draft amendment option.
[07:40] Sarah Miller: Exactly. Also, I'll add two pricing scenarios: conservative (increase reserved to 8 units) and hybrid (keep 4 reserved + 4 burst reserved) for 12/24 month terms.
[07:50] Tom Briscoe: Good. One last question — any IO constraints we should know about for EU private installs? Disk encryption specifics?
[07:57] Diego Ramos: We recommend underlying disks encrypted via your KMS; we support LUKS/TDE patterns and can validate the installer with your infra team. We'll list supported configs.
[08:07] Maya Chen: Thank you. If there's nothing else, let's align on dates in the chat and we'll aim for the run next Tues CET.
[08:14] Priya Patel: I'll send an invite for Tue 2026-06-09 09:00 CET and include the checklist and runbook links.
[08:20] Sarah Miller: Thanks all. Quick note — I'm copying Redwood Legal on the pricing follow-up. We'll reconvene after the benchmark. Appreciate your time.
[08:27] Maya Chen: Thanks Sarah. Bye everyone.
[08:29] (call ends)
